verifier_reason: test_outputs.py::test_clean_html_unchanged: The test failed in the call phase due to an assertion error

items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Constants and functions have clear names, but there are cryptic single-letter names in the core logic (`v`, `s`, `m`, `n`, `ent`). Long regexes such as `TAG_RE`/`ATTR_RE` and the one-line `_decode` substitutions have little explanation.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Policy lives in named constants (`BLOCK_TAGS`, `URL_ATTRS`, `DANGEROUS_SCHEMES`). Functions are short and do one thing each, with a main guard and no debug output. One small duplication: the catch-all scheme regex repeats `DANGEROUS_SCHEMES` without `data:`.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Exceptions are specific (`except (ValueError, OverflowError)`), argv is checked, and I/O uses an explicit encoding with surrogateescape. But tag parsing is regex-based and failed the hidden clean-HTML test, so benign input gets changed. There is also a magic constant `0x110000`.

items.name: Obfuscated vectors neutralised
items.evidence: Attribute matching ignores case (`n.startswith("on")`). `_decode` handles entities, `:`/`&tab;` and stripped control characters. `srcdoc`/`formaction` are always dropped, `xlink:href` is checked, and `base`, `meta refresh`, `iframe`/`object`/`embed`/`template` are removed. The `/` separator is handled by `ATTR_RE`.

items.name: Minimal edits on dirty documents
items.name_zh: 含恶意内容的文档仅做最小修改
items.evidence: Tags are rebuilt only when something changes, so original bytes are kept. But it also removes benign content: whole `noscript`/`template` blocks and all `data:` URLs (including images). This over-removal likely explains the hidden `test_clean_html_unchanged` failure.
